_comment: Scripted vehicles for the live demo. These run on top of whatever random background
traffic is flowing, so the operator sees them in a realistic crowd.
Routes follow real camera_edges, so travel times come from the road graph.
For a deterministic run, turn the random degradation off first:
POST /api/sim/start {"vehiclesPerMinute": 20, "ocrErrorRate": 0, "nullPlateRate": 0}
Otherwise a corrupted or dropped plate read can cost one repeat on the suppression
count, which is realistic but makes a rehearsed number wobble.
1. IDENTITY RECOVERED WITHOUT A PLATE. Read cleanly at CHD_CAM_09 and CHD_CAM_10,
loses its plate entirely at CHD_CAM_11, read again at CHD_CAM_12. Resolution has to
carry it across the gap on appearance and timing alone.
2. BLACKLIST HIT, AND SUPPRESSION. CH01AB1234 is seeded into the blacklist by V9
as a stolen-vehicle report. Five cameras means five matches, which must collapse
into ONE alert carrying repeat_count 5 -- otherwise a wanted vehicle crossing the
city buries the feed under its own alerts.
It is a truck, and CHD_CAM_02 sits in Sector_17, so it also trips the seeded
restricted-zone rule (no heavy vehicles in the commercial core, 08:00-20:00 UTC).
3. CLONE PAIR, part A. Same registration as part B, different colour, and a
different embedding seed so the two genuinely do not look alike. CHD_CAM_09 and
CHD_CAM_04 are 3.6 km apart with no road edge between them; the two are seen ~15 s
apart, which is roughly 860 km/h over the ground.
Part B should therefore raise BOTH:
impossible_speed          -- the same plate cannot be in two places that fast
plate_appearance_mismatch -- the plate matches exactly, the vehicle does not
with related_vehicle_id on each pointing back at part A.

vehicles._comment: 3. CLONE PAIR, part B -- the impostor. Same plate, black, deliberately dissimilar.
